prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation, in which designed molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to remove disease-relevant proteins

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation meets my own test of a game-changer: a completely new idea, chemically simple in principle (a bifunctional molecule that brings a ligase and a target together), with demonstrated consequences. It changes what a small molecule can be asked to do, and it removes proteins that inhibitors cannot touch. It is the only candidate that every one of the eight of us ranked, and that breadth of support matters more to me than the number of first places. Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept in 2001. Crews then drove it for two decades. Ciulli supplied the VHL ligands and the structural, ternary-complex understanding that turned the idea into a rational design discipline. That gives a coherent three-person attribution without stretching anyone's contribution. Independent groups have confirmed the concept, and the clinical pipeline is large.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is timing and attribution. As far as I know no PROTAC is yet an approved drug, so the prize may be a few years early on consequences. The thalidomide-cereblon molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito and others) is a separate, decisive mechanistic discovery that a Crews-Deshaies-Ciulli prize would leave out, and the citation would have to be framed carefully so it does not read as slighting that work. The 2004 ubiquitin prize also needs care. Finally, my own first choice, B026, is a stronger enabling methodology for my field. I discount that preference because I am not neutral about simulation.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing (B007) first as a clear chemical mechanism, deaminase chemistry made programmable, with extensive replication and first clinical results; Liu, Komor and Gaudelli are the core.
responses.response: I agree the science is excellent and Liu is the obvious intellectual centre. I am less comfortable with the three-seat attribution, because Komor and Gaudelli are the lead inventors while the independent Target-AID work of Kondo and Nishida stays outside the prize. It also arrives only six years after the CRISPR prize, and the clinical record is still short. That is the same maturity objection I raise against B011, so I cannot count it against PROTACs and not against base editing. I keep B007 as a serious alternative. It is not a decisive reason to rank it first.

responses.point: Linke places base editing first and ranks phase separation (B046) third as a unifying physical-chemistry idea, while himself calling it somewhat premature given the debate over in vivo relevance.
responses.response: I share the maturity doubt about B046 and would press it harder. The 2009 and 2012 observations are real, but the field still lacks quantitative criteria for what counts as a condensate, and much of the evidence is in vitro droplets. A game-changer must have shown consequences, and I do not think that case is settled. On B007 I agree it is the more mature of the two, but I would not make it a first choice for the reasons I gave Chabes.

responses.point: Aili ranks PROTACs first because it is a new pharmacological modality with clear design rules, a pipeline of degraders, and a validated concept, and he proposes the same Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli trio.
responses.response: I agree with the trio and the logic. I would add two qualifications. He treats the missing regulatory approval as a minor point, but I think it is the main reason the committee might wait. And he mentions Gray and the glue strand only in passing. The molecular-glue work, not the PROTAC work, was what established the cereblon mechanism, so the citation wording has to cover induced proximity without implying the full molecular-glue story is credited.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks nitrogenase (B028) first on structure plus kinetics and spectroscopy, with Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt as the laureates, and ranks PROTACs only fourth because no approved drugs exist and it may be a few years early.
responses.response: Nitrogenase is a deep problem and the carbide structure is a real achievement. But I do not think it passes my game-changer test, because it explains a mechanism in nature and has not yet produced a new capability, and the catalytic cycle is still unresolved. I take his point that PROTACs are possibly early, and I have said so. A concept that has been independently reproduced and has many compounds in late-stage trials seems to me to carry more evidence of consequences than a mechanism still under debate. I would rank B028 below B011.

responses.point: Zou ranks halide perovskites (B047) first for a remarkable efficiency rise in about a decade, but concedes that operational stability and lead content are open and that timing may be slightly early.
responses.response: The efficiency curve is remarkable and the structure-property story is clean. But a six-person credit list, with Miyasaka, Snaith, Park, Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis all having strong claims, makes a three-person attribution hard to defend. The stability problem she names is exactly the consequence test I would apply. I do not think perovskites are ready until durable devices are shown outside the lab.

uncertainties: Whether the first PROTAC or molecular-glue degrader approval has happened or is imminent. I do not know the current regulatory status, and it affects whether the prize is early.
How to word a citation that honours induced-proximity degradation without implying that cereblon molecular-glue discovery (Handa, Ito, Gray) is credited.
Whether the committee will prefer base editing (B007) because of its stronger first-place support, despite the Kondo and Nishida attribution problem.
Whether machine-learned interatomic potentials (B026) are ready, and whether the 2024 prize creates fatigue for computation, given the hard cut of Bartók.
statement.conflict_note: No recusal issue is apparent for B011. My connection to Arieh Warshel and my own work on free-energy and EVB simulation are close to B026 and B018, which is why I rank B026 only as an alternative here. I have no stated personal or institutional link to Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Hyman, Brangwynne or the base-editing candidates in my profile.
